learning_outcomes.text: Explain and illustrate the topics covered during the course using drawings in time and frequency domain, block diagrams, formulas, etc.
Prove the theorems discussed in this course.
Solve exercises related to impulse response, filters, Z-transformation, etc., as seen in the course.
Implement several algorithms from the field of digital signal processing using the C programming language.
Demonstrate correct operation using simulation results/tests.

assessment_rules: The overall grade is on a scale of 1-20, composed of two parts: Digital Signal Processing: Theory and Digital Signal Processing: Lab, each also on a scale of 1-20. For the first examination opportunity, the theory exam is a closed-book written exam and the lab exam is a closed-book practical exam where students implement or complete DSP algorithms in C using lab computers. A non-graphical calculator is allowed for the theory exam. Partial transfers are possible for successful component results (YT5660 - Digital Signal Processing: Theory and YT5661 - Digital Signal Processing: Lab) within the academic year for retakes.
